answers.implementation_then_now: Not rated: no legal duty to advise exists in either year. As context, in 2023 there is no source I opened on information at border posts. In 2025 HRW and the Sala found the roughly 200 US deportees were not told of their right to seek refuge; the Defensoría later reported slow correction. This concerns one group only.

events.article: Habeas corpus on US deportees at CATEM
events.what_changed: Chamber found ~200 third-country nationals were held without an individualised resolution and ordered individual reasoned acts. A group-specific breach, not a change in the law.
events.passage: la privación de libertad sin resolución individualizada, la falta de información sobre su estatus migratorio, la restricción de comunicación con el exterior

answers.implementation_then_now: 2023: ordinary deportations and expulsions go through individual DGME resolutions, reviewable by habeas corpus/amparo; I found no 2023-period source documenting systematic breach, so 'Usually' rests on the law and the starting coder's assessment. 2026: same pattern, with one documented 2025 breach affecting about 200 US deportees. This did not shift general practice.

provisions.article: Arts. 65, 222 (no appeal against rejection and deportation)

answers.implementation_then_now: 2023 and 2026: expulsion of residents follows the evidence and suspensive appeal stages; deportation of irregular migrants gives only an oral hearing before DGME and no administrative appeal (art. 222), so review depends on habeas corpus. The 2025 CATEM case showed failures in access to information and individual decisions for ~200 US deportees. No source I opened documents 2023 practice directly, so the rating is carried over.
